summaryPoints: South Africa recovered from early pressure in the first innings, anchored by Dean Elgar's resolute 140 to post 308.
New Zealand replied strongly with 341, powered by Kane Williamson's commanding century (130) to swing the contest.
South Africa posted 224/6 in their second innings, shifting match momentum decisively through crucial partnerships.
A resilient final-day rearguard ensured the match concluded in a fiercely contested draw.

scorecards.inningsCommentary: South Africa commenced their first innings at University Oval, aiming to set an imposing baseline total. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 140 from Dean Elgar, complemented by a commanding 126-run stand between Dean Elgar and Francois Plessis that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 2.5 RPO. New Zealand's bowling response was spearheaded by Trent Boult (4/62), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Concluding at 308/10 (122.4 ov), South Africa posted a competitive total, ensuring a closely matched contest.

scorecards.inningsCommentary: Entering the third innings with the match balance in flux, South Africa sought to extend their lead and set a decisive fourth-innings target. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 89 from Dean Elgar, complemented by a commanding 80-run stand between Francois Plessis and Dean Elgar that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 2.19 RPO. Neil Wagner (2/56) maintained tight lines for New Zealand, creating intermittent chances in an otherwise demanding fielding effort. South Africa's total of 224/6 (101.6 ov) closed their second innings, cementing a formidable target and transferring immense pressure onto the opposition.

summaryTab.matchStory: South Africa recovered from early pressure in the first innings, anchored by Dean Elgar's resolute 140 to post 308. New Zealand replied strongly with 341, powered by Kane Williamson's commanding century (130) to swing the contest. South Africa posted 224/6 in their second innings, shifting match momentum decisively through crucial partnerships. A resilient final-day rearguard ensured the match concluded in a fiercely contested draw.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at University Oval commenced with high tactical intensity as South Africa posted 308/10 (122.4 ov) in their opening innings. In response, New Zealand countered with 341/10 (114.3 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Century: Dean Elgar 140 (299b), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Dean Elgar delivered a masterclass for South Africa (229 Runs), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Match Drawn 45%) and allowing Match Drawn to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, New Zealand faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Match Drawn's bowling unit, bolstered by Neil Wagner (32 Runs & 5 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Match drawn in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Match Drawn's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While New Zealand produced fighting phases, Match Drawn won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
